skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Guides agents through creating isolated Git worktrees with directory selection, ignore checks, setup steps, and baseline verification.
skill.summary: Create isolated Git worktrees for feature work while preserving the current workspace.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, literal shell examples, documented worktree paths, and /dev/null redirects. No prompt injection or secret access evidence was found. The main residual risks are automatic dependency setup and repository commits before explicit user review.

remediation.issue: Automatic package setup can execute project-controlled scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before install, build, or download commands. Prefer frozen or lockfile-aware installs when the project supports them.

remediation.issue: The skill may commit .gitignore changes without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Show the proposed .gitignore diff and ask before committing. Include the exact commit message in the confirmation request.

remediation.issue: Branch and directory names are interpolated into Git commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate branch names and worktree locations before command execution. Reject empty values and option-like names that start with a dash.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Dependency Setup Can Execute Project Code
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to run package manager setup commands automatically for Node.js, Rust, Python, and Go projects. These commands can download dependencies and execute project-controlled scripts during installation or build steps.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 105-118 directly list npm install, cargo build, pip install, poetry install, and go mod download as automatic setup actions. These commands are legitimate but can execute untrusted project code.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Changes May Be Committed Without Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: When a project-local worktree directory is not ignored, the skill tells the agent to edit .gitignore, commit the change, and continue. This can modify repository history before the user reviews the diff.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to add a .gitignore line and commit the change before creating the worktree. The intent is operational safety, but it still changes repository state.

content.value_statement: Feature work can disrupt an active workspace and hide baseline failures. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safer Git worktree setup.
actual_capabilities: Chooses .worktrees, worktrees, or a global worktree path from project context.
Checks project-local worktree directories with git check-ignore before creation.
Creates a Git worktree and branch with git worktree add.
Detects common project manifests for Node.js, Rust, Python, and Go setup.
Runs baseline tests and asks before continuing when tests fail.
Reports the final worktree path and readiness status.
limitations: Assumes Git is installed and the current directory belongs to a repository.
Does not clean up worktrees after a branch is finished.
May run dependency setup commands that execute project-defined scripts.
Requires user judgment when baseline tests fail or setup commands are unsafe.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Work Safely
use_cases.description: Create a separate worktree before changing code, preserving the current branch and working directory.

use_cases.title: Prepare Parallel Implementation Tasks
use_cases.description: Set up branch-specific workspaces so multiple plans can progress without branch switching conflicts.

use_cases.title: Verify a Clean Baseline
use_cases.description: Run setup and tests in a fresh worktree before attributing failures to new implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single feature branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-git-worktrees skill to create an isolated worktree for my next feature. Ask before making repository changes.

prompt_templates.title: Respect Project Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Use existing workspace rules and directory preferences.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-git-worktrees skill and follow this repository's existing worktree directory convention. Verify the directory is ignored first.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Worktree and Baseline Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up a branch and check the starting test state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-git-worktrees skill for a new branch, then run the project baseline tests and report any failures before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Feature Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for multiple independent changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-git-worktrees skill to plan isolated worktrees for two independent features. Confirm setup commands before running package managers.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for an authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the project worktree directory, verifies ignore rules, creates the branch workspace, runs setup, and reports readiness.

output_examples.input: The baseline tests fail after worktree setup.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the failing test command, reports that the baseline is not clean, and asks whether to investigate or continue.
The assistant offers a project-local hidden directory or a global configuration directory and waits for the user choice.

best_practices: Confirm project-local worktree directories are ignored before creating the workspace.
Ask before running dependency installation in unfamiliar or untrusted repositories.
Record baseline test results before starting implementation work.
anti_patterns: Creating a worktree in a tracked project directory.
Running package manager installs without checking trust and user intent.
Continuing after baseline test failures without user approval.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps create isolated Git worktrees so feature work does not disturb the current workspace.

faq.question: Does it choose the worktree directory automatically?
faq.answer: It first checks existing project conventions, then reads CLAUDE.md, then asks the user when no preference exists.

faq.question: Why does it check gitignore rules?
faq.answer: Project-local worktree directories should be ignored to avoid accidentally tracking nested worktree files.

faq.question: Can it run project setup commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run detected setup commands, but users should confirm installs in unfamiliar repositories.

faq.question: Does it clean up old worktrees?
faq.answer: No. Cleanup is outside this skill and should be handled by a finishing or branch cleanup workflow.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for agentic coding tools that can inspect repositories and run Git commands.
